items.keyReason: Nobody is singular, so knows agrees with it. Everyone, someone, and anybody are also singular; have, are, and need do not agree with those subjects. The intervening prepositional phrases do not change the subject number.
items.rule: Singular indefinite pronouns such as everyone, someone, nobody, and anybody take singular present-tense verbs even when a plural noun follows in a prepositional phrase.

A.reason: The nearby plural trails and the plural meaning of everyone can attract an incorrect plural verb, though the mismatch is conventional and easy to spot.

B.reason: The nearby plural lockers offers an attraction cue; the wrong auxiliary are is conspicuous with someone.

D.reason: The nearby plural batteries offers an attraction cue, but need repeats the same missing singular inflection used in A.

items.keyReason: The kettle and the toaster is a compound subject joined by and, so the plural verb work agrees. The other options have two separately determined nouns joined by and but use singular is, belongs, or has.
items.rule: Two distinct singular nouns joined by and form a plural subject and take a plural present-tense verb.

A.reason: Is is a clear singular mismatch with two separately named objects; there is no intervening material or competing number cue.

crossItemReview.explanation: Both ask the learner to choose the sole correct full sentence among four unrelated scenes by finding the subject and checking a single present-tense verb. Q01 tests singular indefinite pronouns with intervening phrases; Q02 tests plural and-compound subjects. Thus the underlying rules differ, while the answer-selection method and option construction repeat.
crossItemReview.qualityImplication: As a two-item set, the rule coverage is distinct, but the repeated one-correct/three-same-error format reduces variety. Q02 needs more demanding yet unambiguous distractors to meet the 2-3 target.
